title: The "Sportsman Musician" and European racial attitudes
summary: He skied and swam while others drank, and thought racial attitudes in France and Switzerland far better than in America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I wasn't pretty young in those days, you know. I was the youngest in the band, and they would say... They called me the Sportsman Musician. You know, while the

guys were in the bar throwing their head back, I would be skiing, I'd be doing everything else. And it paid off, because I outlasted all of them! While they were drinking, you know, every day, I was eating up a breeze or going swimming or something like that. I was really enjoying it.
How did you find the attitudes in Europe as compared...?

When you talk about that, it still almost surprises me a little bit that it was better, because France and England, for instance, were both big empires, colonial empires. Now, you know, in London, well, there were always people coming from the colonies with their racial prejudice... That was basically the reason why there was occasional troubles in London at hotels, because of all these people coming from South Africa bringing their attitudes. But France, which also had a big empire, that really seemed much better, didn't it. I mean, very un-prejudiced about race and everything.
Well, you must realize they always had an influx of travelers. So I mean, we were quick to recognize this and adapt ourselves to the customs of the country which
they inhabit, you know. I don't want to get into an area which I know so little of. But their Foreign Service was much more superior than ours.
